building.quote: CITY OF ALBUQUERQUE AMENDMENTS TO THE NEW MEXICO BUILDING CODE, AS ADOPTED BY THE CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRIES DIVISION OF THE STATE OF NEW MEXICO WITH AN EFFECTIVE DATE OF January 1, 2025 [...] The 2021 New Mexico Plumbing Code; including Appendixes A, B, C, D, E, F, I, K, and L; [...] The 2021 New Mexico Commercial Building Code including Appendix Chapters C, E, G, H, I, and J as amended, and all other Appendices as written. [...] The 2021 New Mexico Existing Building Code; [...] Title 14, Chapter 5 of the New Mexico Building Code has been deleted and replaced with Chapter 1, on the following pages. Sections from various other parts of the Technical Codes have been amended, added, or deleted.
building.amendments_note: The city's changes to the New Mexico Commercial Building Code are limited to Chapter 1 (administration, replaced by the city's own), Chapter 18 (frost depth 16 inches), Chapter 30 (elevators) and Chapter 35 (two added standards). Chapters 8 (interior finishes, the HDPE fire test), 10 (occupant load), 11 (accessibility) and 29 (toilet counts) carry no city amendment, so the state pack's text on them stands. Section 102.1: "Buildings, structures and their building service equipment to which additions, alterations or repairs are made shall comply with the 2021 New Mexico Existing Building Code." Section 110.2: "Occupant load shall be defined and determined by the method set forth in Table 1004.5 of the International Building Code, as amended by the New Mexico Commercial Building Code."

scheduled_change.what: The State of New Mexico's 2024 New Mexico Plumbing Code (14.8.2 NMAC) took effect August 1, 2026, and state permits may use the 2021 code only until January 1, 2027. Albuquerque's Uniform Administrative Code, 2024 Edition, still names the 2021 New Mexico Plumbing Code; no city update was found on the city's codes page. The toilet counts are not affected: both state editions and the city amendment send the reader to the New Mexico Commercial Building Code.

fixtures.city_amends_note: Albuquerque's Uniform Administrative Code (2024 Edition) has no amendment to Chapter 29 of the New Mexico Commercial Building Code. Its plumbing amendments delete the Uniform Plumbing Code's Section 422.0 and Table 422.1 and refer to the New Mexico Commercial Building Code, the same result as the state rule. The state pack's table, urinal sentence and worked examples stand. The only city text on urinals is on nonwater urinals (Section 412.1.1: listed, with a water line roughed in), which doesn't change the count.

permit.repair_definition_quote: REPAIR is the patching, restoration, or renewal of materials, elements, equipment, or fixtures for the sole purpose of maintaining such materials, elements, equipment, or fixtures in sound working condition.
permit.partitions_named_note: The list names only "non-fixed and moveable" partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches high. Toilet partitions anchored to the floor, wall or ceiling are not named, and the list doesn't say whether replacing them is "similar finish work" or a repair under $1,000.

restrooms_city.note: No city rule found. The city's building code amendments (Uniform Administrative Code, 2024 Edition, read in full for restroom, toilet and sign text) add nothing on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms. Two web searches found no Albuquerque ordinance on the subject. The Code of Ordinances itself (codelibrary.amlegal.com) returned HTTP 403 to automated access and was not read. One search result (a news report, not read on an official page) says the council widened the city's Human Rights Ordinance in 2024 to cover gender identity; nothing in it was reported about restroom signs or design.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Albuquerque job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the New Mexico rules the city enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Albuquerque offices, schools, hospitals and university buildings, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Albuquerque applies New Mexico's building rules, which set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Albuquerque requires a permit to alter or repair a building and lists the work that needs none. The list covers painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work, movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches, and repairs worth less than $1,000. It doesn't name toilet partitions fixed to the floor or wall, so ask the city's Building Safety Division (505-924-3320) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Albuquerque uses New Mexico's rules without changing the counts. They count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: they may replace up to half of the men's toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, so you can buy fewer men's stalls and add urinal screens.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. New Mexico's rules don't say clearly whether a small business may have one shared restroom, so ask Albuquerque's Building Safety Division.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Albuquerque's Building Safety Division sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Albuquerque issues commercial building permits only to a general contractor licensed by the State of New Mexico. New Mexico requires a state contractor license for construction work. Partition installation is not named in the state's list of license classes, so installers typically hold a general building license (GB-98) or the miscellaneous specialty license (GS-29); confirm which applies with the state's Construction Industries Division. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: The contractor needs a New Mexico contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, city, county and school projects over $60,000, New Mexico law requires at least the wage and benefits the state sets each year for each trade. For a carpenter on building work in Bernalillo County the 2026 rate is $32.12 an hour plus $14.28 in benefits, and the employer also pays $0.60 an hour into an apprenticeship fund.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Gross receipts tax:** 7.625% in Albuquerque: the 4.875% state rate plus 2.75% in local taxes. Rates normally change only on July 1.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals, university and research buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are cleaned many times a day.
sources: - Codes Albuquerque enforces: City of Albuquerque, Building Safety Division, [Current Building Codes](https://www.cabq.gov/planning/building-safety-division/current-building-codes) and the [Uniform Administrative Code of the City of Albuquerque, 2024 Edition](https://www.cabq.gov/planning/documents/2024-uac-adopted.pdf) (City of Albuquerque amendments to the New Mexico building codes, effective January 1, 2025: it adopts the 2021 New Mexico Commercial Building Code, the 2021 New Mexico Existing Building Code and the 2021 New Mexico Plumbing Code, and amends Chapters 1, 18, 30 and 35 of the building code only). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts in Albuquerque: [Uniform Administrative Code of the City of Albuquerque, 2024 Edition](https://www.cabq.gov/planning/documents/2024-uac-adopted.pdf), amendments to the 2021 New Mexico Plumbing Code, Chapter 4 (Section 422.0 and Table 422.1 of the Uniform Plumbing Code deleted, with a reference to the New Mexico Commercial Building Code); no city amendment to Chapter 29 of the building code. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Permits in Albuquerque: [Uniform Administrative Code of the City of Albuquerque, 2024 Edition](https://www.cabq.gov/planning/documents/2024-uac-adopted.pdf), Sections 109.1 (permits required), 109.2.1 (work exempt from a building permit) and 111.1 (permits issued only to contractors licensed by the state's Construction Industries Division); Building Safety Division, [Permits](https://www.cabq.gov/planning/building-safety-division/permits) (505-924-3320). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Wages on public jobs in Bernalillo County: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions, Labor Relations Division, [Prevailing Wage Rates, Type "B" General Building, effective January 1, 2026](https://www.dws.nm.gov/Portals/0/DM/LaborRelations/Prevailing_Wage_Poster_B_2026.pdf) (Carpenter/Lather: base rate $32.12, fringe rate $14.28, apprenticeship $0.60; one rate statewide except Los Alamos County), linked from its [Public Works page](https://www.dws.nm.gov/Public-Works). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Gross receipts tax rate in Albuquerque: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department, Gross Receipts and Compensating Tax Rate Schedule, effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 (location code 02-100, Albuquerque, 7.6250%; state rate 4.875%), as printed in the Department's [GRT Filer's Kit, July 2026 to June 2027](https://klvg4oyd4j.execute-api.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/prod/PublicFiles/34821a9573ca43e7b06dfad20f5183fd/6b9a5047-3e5a-45c4-9986-4685eda09921/2026%20July%20to%20June%202027%20GRT%20Filer%27s%20Kit.pdf); current rates are on its [location code and tax rate map page](https://www.tax.newmexico.gov/governments/gross-receipts-location-code-and-tax-rate-map/). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1-2017 as referenced by Chapter 11 and Appendix E of the 2021 New Mexico Commercial Building Code (14.7.2 NMAC, the 2021 International Building Code with New Mexico amendments; Section 803.9, Table 1004.5, Section 2902.1 and Table 2902.1); Uniform Administrative Code of the City of Albuquerque, 2024 Edition (City of Albuquerque amendments to the New Mexico building codes, effective January 1, 2025; Sections 109.1, 109.2 and 111.1); 2021 New Mexico Plumbing Code (the 2021 Uniform Plumbing Code) with Albuquerque amendments; the state's 2024 New Mexico Plumbing Code (14.8.2 NMAC, the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code with New Mexico amendments) took effect August 1, 2026 and is the only edition for state permits after January 1, 2027; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of anchored toilet partitions in a commercial restroom needs an Albuquerque building permit (Building Safety Division, 505-924-3320, option 2 for plan review).

Albuquerque's Uniform Administrative Code (2024 Edition, effective January 1, 2025) names the 2021 New Mexico Plumbing Code, while the state's 2024 edition becomes the only one for state permits on January 1, 2027. Ask the Building Safety Division which edition it applies after that date; the toilet counts are the same either way.

The ordinance that adopted the 2024 Edition of the Uniform Administrative Code was not found: the city's codes page links only the 2022 ordinance (O-2022-024). Ask the City Clerk for the enactment number.

No city ordinance on restroom signs or all-gender rooms was found, but Albuquerque's Code of Ordinances (American Legal) blocks automated access: check it once in a browser, including the Human Rights Ordinance.

Gross receipts tax: the 7.625% rate is from the July 2026 to June 2027 schedule, accurate as of June 1, 2026; recheck on the Taxation and Revenue Department's rate page before launch and each July. The city and county shares of the 2.75% local part were not read.
Public works wage rates are reset each January 1: replace the 2026 carpenter rate ($32.12 plus $14.28) with the 2027 rate when the Department of Workforce Solutions posts it.

The city's Commercial Alterations handout, the source of the contractor rule, still lists the 2015 codes (it is dated 2020); the rule itself is confirmed by Section 111.1 of the Uniform Administrative Code, which says any contractor licensed by the state's Construction Industries Division, not only a GB-98 holder.
